sources.title: Construction output in Great Britain: May 2026
sources.verified_claim: ONS estimates construction output grew 1.6% in the three months to May 2026 while monthly output fell 0.8%, and flags revisions and a corrected historical data error. National output movements are market context, not a parcel-specific viability result.

sources.title: Output in the construction industry
sources.verified_claim: ONS publishes monthly current-price and chained-volume construction output with quality measures and revisions. Aggregate output data cannot substitute for a scheme cost plan or parcel residual valuation.

sources.title: Construction output price indices
sources.verified_claim: The ONS OPI dataset is its best estimate of construction output price inflation through March 2026. Index inflation is a national proxy and is not an exact build-cost quotation for the sample parcels.

sources.title: Building materials and components statistics: June 2026
sources.verified_claim: DBT publishes official price indices and supply data for selected construction materials. Material statistics are sector evidence and do not establish procurement cost or availability for a specific scheme.

sources.title: Development Viability Guidance
sources.verified_claim: The consultation page describes draft Development Viability London Plan Guidance for assessing viability information and maximising planning contributions. Draft/consultation status is retained and it is not treated as an adopted site valuation.

sources.title: Fees for planning applications
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The consultation records fees applicable from 1 April 2026 alongside proposed national default fees and other reforms. Proposed fees are not treated as already implemented and application fees are only one component of development cost.

sources.title: Fees for planning applications: government response
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Government published its response covering national default fees, local fee setting and next steps. Policy response does not determine total project viability or a sample parcel's eventual application fee without scheme details.

sources.title: Fees for planning applications
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: The guidance explains nationally set planning fees and annual inflation-linked increases. Fee methodology is a statutory process input, not evidence that development on a sample parcel is financially viable.
